title: performance(canary): add automated detection and hysteresis-based rollout guards
author: Aisha Thompson
description: Motivation: deploys of new model variants or runtime changes occasionally introduce subtle latency regressions that slip through unit and integration tests. This PR introduces an automated performance canary detector with hysteresis-based rollout guards to detect latency and throughput regressions during canary rollouts and automatically halt/rollback traffic if thresholds are violated. Summary of change: 1) a new perf-canary-detector service that consumes per-route token-level histograms and 95/99p latency windows from the metrics pipeline; 2) adaptive thresholding using baseline windows with configurable sensitivity and hysteresis to avoid flapping; 3) integration with the rollout controller to pause traffic shifting and emit actionable alerts; 4) new config schema for canary policies in deployments.yaml and Console UI hooks; 5) unit and e2e tests plus perf canary integration test harness. Backwards compatibility: existing rollout configs without canary_policy are unaffected; detector defaults to monitoring-only mode unless a policy is present. Rollout guard behavior: when the detector observes sustained 99th percentile latency regression > threshold for the configured window and after hysteresis conditions are met, it transitions rollout to PAUSED and posts an action to the rollout controller which triggers automatic rollback after configurable grace period. Implementation notes: detector computes delta over baseline using exponential EWMA for stable baselines, applies a noise floor for low-QPS routes, and requires N consecutive windows to trip to satisfy hysteresis. The policy supports severity levels (warning/critical) and multi-metric checks (latency + qps drop). Tests: added unit tests for EWMA and hysteresis logic, integration test that spins up a small canary traffic simulation using the perf-canary lab harness, and a smoke test validating rollback path. Deployment: feature gated behind feature flag perf_canary_autodetect; rollout to canary infra for 2 weeks before full enablement. Related work: builds on ENG-312 (metrics histogram refactor) and uses new tracing tags added in ENG-399.

review_comments: Diego: Can you explain how the baseline is computed for low-QPS routes? Concern about false positives.
Rina: Config schema looks good but we should keep default sensitivity conservative. Also request validation added to CLI.
Samir: Consider adding a debug endpoint to force a manual pause/resume for incident response.
Diego: Is the detector horizontally scalable? What are memory characteristics for many routes?
author_responses: Author: For low-QPS routes we apply a noise floor and require a minimum sample count before evaluating thresholds; details added to algorithm doc and unit tests.
Author: lowered default sensitivity and added CLI validation in deployments schema; included a console warning about conservative defaults.
Author: added a /debug/canary-control endpoint behind RBAC and feature flag for manual pause/resume; documented in runbook.
Author: detector shards metrics by route-hash and uses streaming summarization; added a section in README about memory and suggested shard counts for large orgs.
release_notes: Add automated performance canary detector and rollout guards. Feature gated behind perf_canary_autodetect. Default sensitivity conservative to avoid false positives. Administrators can configure hysteresis and grace periods per deployment.
notes: Follow-up tasks: 1) dashboards for canary-detector per-route insights (ENG-442); 2) add RBAC audit hooks for manual interventions; 3) schedule staged rollout of feature flag to 20% of orgs next week.
